notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order grouped by theme, not a chronology; surah order is not time order. Saba is told in seven ayat. The draft states them; where Saba lay and who ruled it are not in the ayat.

claims.statement_en: The Quran says that there was a sign for Saba in their dwelling place: gardens on the right and on the left.
They were told to eat of the provision of their Lord and to give thanks to Him, for theirs was a good land and a forgiving Lord.
God placed between them and the towns He had blessed visible towns, and measured the journey between them.
They were told to travel in them by night and by day in safety.

chapters.summary_md: The Quran says that Saba had a sign in their dwelling place, gardens on the right and on the left [c1]. They were told to eat of the provision of their Lord and give thanks to Him [c2], and to travel in safety between visible towns [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: The Quran says that there was a sign for Saba in their dwelling place: gardens on the right and on the left [c1]. They were told to eat of the provision of their Lord and to give thanks to Him, for theirs was a good land and a forgiving Lord [c2]. God placed between them and the towns He had blessed visible towns, and measured the journey between them [c3]. They were told to travel in them by night and by day in safety [c4].
chapters.deep_md:
- The Quran says that there was a sign for Saba in their dwelling place: gardens on the right and on the left (34:15) [c1].
- They were told to eat of the provision of their Lord and to give thanks to Him, for theirs was a good land and a forgiving Lord (34:15) [c2].
- God placed between them and the towns He had blessed visible towns, and measured the journey between them (34:18) [c3].
- They were told to travel in them by night and by day in safety (34:18) [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The people of Saba had gardens on the right and on the left [c1]. They were told to eat what their Lord provided and to thank Him [c2]. They could travel safely from town to town [c3][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The first ayat give the favours before the account of what the people did with them [c1][c2][c3]. One reading is that gratitude is the response the passage asks for [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where Saba was, when it flourished, who ruled it or how many people lived there; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: the Arabic of 34:15 uses a dual form for the gardens; the draft says gardens on the right and on the left.
- Not established: which towns are the towns He had blessed, and where the visible towns stood; the ayat do not say.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Yemen, Marib and the dam later accounts connect with Saba; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: They turned away, and God sent on them the flood of the Arim.
He replaced their gardens with gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote trees.
The Quran says that this was their recompense for their disbelief, and asks whether any is recompensed in this way but the ungrateful.
They said, our Lord, make the distances between our journeys longer, and they wronged themselves.
God made them tales and scattered them completely.
The Quran says that in this are signs for every patient and grateful person.
Iblis proved true his opinion about them, and they followed him except a group of the believers.
Iblis had no authority over them, but it was so that God might know who believes in the Hereafter and who is in doubt about it, and your Lord is a guardian over all things.

chapters.summary_md: The Quran says that the people turned away, and God sent on them the flood of the Arim and replaced their gardens [c1][c2]. It calls this their recompense for disbelief and says that God made them tales and scattered them [c3][c5].
chapters.body_md: They turned away, and God sent on them the flood of the Arim [c1]. He replaced their gardens with gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote trees [c2]. The Quran says that this was their recompense for their disbelief, and asks whether any is recompensed in this way but the ungrateful [c3]. They said, our Lord, make the distances between our journeys longer, and they wronged themselves [c4]. God made them tales and scattered them completely [c5]. The Quran says that in this are signs for every patient and grateful person [c6]. Iblis proved true his opinion about them, and they followed him except a group of the believers [c7]. Iblis had no authority over them, but it was so that God might know who believes in the Hereafter and who is in doubt about it, and your Lord is a guardian over all things [c8].
chapters.deep_md:
- They turned away, and God sent on them the flood of the Arim (34:16) [c1].
- He replaced their gardens with gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote trees (34:16) [c2].
- The Quran says that this was their recompense for their disbelief, and asks whether any is recompensed in this way but the ungrateful (34:17) [c3].
- They said, our Lord, make the distances between our journeys longer, and they wronged themselves (34:19) [c4].
- God made them tales and scattered them completely (34:19) [c5].
- The Quran says that in this are signs for every patient and grateful person (34:19) [c6].
- Iblis proved true his opinion about them, and they followed him except a group of the believers (34:20) [c7].
- Iblis had no authority over them, but it was so that God might know who believes in the Hereafter and who is in doubt about it, and your Lord is a guardian over all things (34:21) [c8].
chapters.kids_md: The people turned away from thanking God [c1]. A great flood came, and their gardens were changed [c1][c2]. The Quran says that there are signs in this for everyone who is patient and thankful [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage ends with signs for the patient and grateful, after the account of those who were ungrateful [c3][c6]. One reading is that the ayat set the loss of a land of favour beside the call to give thanks [c1][c3][c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the Arim is a word read in more than one way (a dam, a flood, a kind of rain); the draft keeps the word as the ayah gives it.
- Not established: the draft does not say when the flood came, or how many lives it cost; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: the sense of the plants named in 34:16 (the bitter fruit, tamarisk and lote) is read in more than one way.
- Not established: how Iblis proved true his opinion, or what the group of believers did; the ayat say only that they followed him except a group.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the account of the dam of Marib, the emigration of the tribes and the date; none is used here.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about Saba. None is used in this draft.

Wording a scholar should check first: 34:16 (the Arim, and the plants), 34:19 (tales, scattered completely), 34:15 (the dual form of the gardens), 34:19 (make the distances longer), 34:21 (that We might know).
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Marib, the dam of Marib, the scattering of the tribes of the south and the dates; none is used.
